name: Casluh
overview: Casluh is a male figure mentioned in Scripture as a son of Mizraim. He is noted specifically for being the ancestor from whom the Philistines originated, according to Genesis 10:14. Beyond this, there is limited information about his tribe or other attributes.
namesAndTitles: The name Casluh appears as a proper name in the biblical text, with no specific meaning or divine origin indicated. The Scripture simply records this name without additional explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Casluh as a son of Mizraim, establishing his place within the genealogical line descending from Mizraim. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Casluh's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his role as the progenitor of the Philistines, a people who play an important role throughout the Old Testament. As a descendant of Mizraim, Casluh represents a branch of the nations that emerged after the Flood, contributing to the broader understanding of the nations' origins in God's providential plan. His mention helps trace the lineage and movements of peoples known from biblical history.
